decision: Implement in a new worktree from origin/main
why: The checkpoint worktree contains uncommitted evidence harness files and must remain untouched
result: Preserves the v0.3.4 checkpoint and historical #87 checkout

decision: Use a single-use accepted-position token with one CSS pixel event tolerance
why: Solution Gate probes refuted requested-value and strict-readback tokens after a second browser clamp
result: Assumes the reported clamp discrepancy is bounded to one CSS pixel

decision: Assign scrollHeight instead of subtracting rounded getters
why: The browser owns the actual maximum scroll offset and clamps oversized assignments synchronously
result: Bottom requests no longer depend on two rounded layout getters

decision: Model requested, accepted, and event positions independently
why: The regression survives a synchronous read-back when layout reclamps before event delivery
result: The strict-readback mutant must fail for the second-clamp assertion

decision: Emulate browser scroll clamping in jsdom
why: jsdom accepts out-of-range scrollTop values and cannot validate bottom ownership without an explicit clamp
result: The existing exact-bottom test continues to assert the browser contract rather than jsdom behavior

decision: Require separate tests to kill strict-event and requested-token mutants
why: A green regression test is insufficient unless it fails for each removed mechanism
result: Strict equality failed the second-clamp test and requested value failed the accepted-position test

decision: Run Electron 43.4.0 directly on a headless Weston Wayland compositor
why: The issue is specific to Electron Chromium Linux Wayland and Xvfb cannot exercise that compositor
result: The probe fails if Electron, Chromium, DPR, or Wayland identity differs

decision: Require the unfixed base to reproduce in the same workflow
why: A fixed-only green cannot prove the remote runner reaches the reported failure family
result: The matrix restores only wterm.ts from 4a73024 and expects at least one failed geometry
